name: Mixture-of-Experts with Expert Choice Routing
authors: Zhou, Lepikhin, Klyushko, Dettmers, et al. (Google)
problem: Top-k gating gives every token the same number of experts regardless of how important the token is, and load imbalance leaves some experts under-trained and under-specialized.
mechanism: INVERTS THE ROUTING DIRECTION: instead of each token selecting its top-k experts, each EXPERT selects its top-k tokens. Each expert therefore gets a FIXED BUCKET SIZE (a constant, known compute cost) while each token receives a VARIABLE number of experts - so an easy token can be handled by one expert and a hard token by eight. The fixed bucket is also what removes the load-imbalance problem that makes token-choice routing expensive to serve.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): systematically studied against Switch Transformer top-1 and GShard top-2 gating AT THE SAME COMPUTATIONAL RESOURCES, and improves TRAINING CONVERGENCE TIME BY MORE THAN 2x; higher performance fine-tuning 11 selected GLUE/SuperGLUE tasks at the same computational cost; and at lower activation cost it beats the T5 dense model on 7 of 11 tasks. COMPRESSION RATIO: not applicable (a routing scheme). Note the caveat that matters for serving: fixed bucket size means the dispatch buffers are static and computationally predictable, which is precisely the property token-choice routing lacks.
